Discover an OAuth authorization server

Source: R/providers__oauth_discovery.R
oauth_provider_oauth_discover.Rd

Fetch RFC 8414 metadata for an OAuth authorization-code provider. The metadata location inserts /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server before the issuer's path. A terminal slash is removed for that request; the returned issuer must still match the caller's issuer exactly, including its terminal slash.

Usage

oauth_provider_oauth_discover(
  issuer,
  name = NULL,
  use_pkce = TRUE,
  token_auth_style = NULL,
  allowed_token_types = "Bearer",
  ...
)

Arguments

issuer

Exact OAuth authorization-server issuer URL, including its scheme, path and any terminal slash. Supply the issuer identifier rather than a metadata-document URL.

name

Optional friendly provider name. Defaults to the issuer hostname

use_pkce

Logical, whether to use PKCE for this provider. Defaults to TRUE. Public clients require PKCE. Setting FALSE also prevents automatic selection of public-client authentication; a confidential-client method must be available or explicitly configured instead.

token_auth_style

Authentication style for token requests: "header" (client_secret_basic), "body" (client_secret_post), or "public" (public client; send client_id only). The alias "none" is also accepted for "public". If NULL (default), it is inferred conservatively from discovery: "header" (client_secret_basic) is preferred, followed by "body" (client_secret_post), then "public" if none is advertised and PKCE is enabled. Set token_auth_style = "public" explicitly for a public client registration. JWT methods ("client_secret_jwt", "private_key_jwt") and mTLS methods ("tls_client_auth", "self_signed_tls_client_auth") must be selected explicitly. See oauth_provider() for the supported methods and their credentials.

allowed_token_types

Character vector of allowed token types for access tokens issued by this provider. Defaults to 'Bearer'

...

Additional oauth_provider() settings. OIDC settings and relaxed issuer matching are not accepted by this OAuth-only helper.

Value

An OAuthProvider configured from the authorization-server metadata.

Details

This helper requires support for the code flow and configures OAuth-only behavior: no automatic openid scope, OIDC nonce, ID-token validation or UserInfo request. It retains the discovery transport, endpoint, host, PKCE, client authentication, PAR, DPoP and mTLS checks. JWKS is optional; an advertised JWKS URL still undergoes the normal URL and host checks.

Supply an issuer identifier, rather than a metadata-document URL. This helper does not fall back to another discovery location and does not verify signed metadata. Use oauth_provider_oidc_discover() for OpenID Connect.

See also

oauth_provider(), oauth_provider_oidc_discover()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Requires your service's issuer URL and a registered public OAuth client.
provider <- oauth_provider_oauth_discover(
  issuer = "https://auth.example.com",
  token_auth_style = "public"
)
client <- oauth_client(
  provider = provider,
  client_id = "your-client-id",
  redirect_uri = "http://127.0.0.1:8100/callback"
)
} # }
